title: Embed safety contracts in PRD for kernel regression, autoscale backpressure, and graceful fallback
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
This ticket updates the runtime PRD to encode postmortem-derived safety contracts focused on two recurring incident classes: (1) kernel performance regressions that present as elevated p95/p99 latencies and token-time spikes, and (2) autoscaler backpressure / cold-start storms that cause cascading request queueing. The goal is to convert incident playbook actions into unambiguous product requirements (contracts) that are testable and enforceable by engineering and SRE during rollout.

Scope changes:
- Add explicit SLAs and degradation contracts for compatible fallback model variants (latency / quality trade-offs).
- Require a fast-path circuit-breaker: runtime must support service-level circuit config allowing immediate routing to warm pools or compatible smaller quantized variants when model kernel regressions exceed threshold.
- Define autoscale backpressure acceptance tests: synthetic ramp that verifies warm-pool warm-up time, autoscale cooldown, and queue-shed behavior under sustained surge.
- Require gating criteria for rollouts: new kernels or optimized operator changes must pass the safety contract test-suite before canary reaches >10% traffic.

Why this is different from existing PRD updates:
Previous PRDs captured fallback and rollback in general terms. This update encodes measurable contracts (thresholds, synthetic tests, rollout gates) and ties them to release criteria, dashboards, and runbooks so that SRE and Release Engineering can verify before/after every rollout.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Tight safety gates increase release friction but materially reduce incident blast radius. We propose automated synthetic verification to keep developer velocity.
- Fallback to smaller/quantized model variants may increase error rate for edge prompts; acceptance criteria include targeted QA on representative prompt sets to bound quality regressions.

Acceptance test summary (high level): must pass all of the following for the PRD to be accepted and merged into the main runtime PRD:
1) Regression detection test: inject small latency perturbation in kernel path; system detects and flips to fallback within configured SLO 95th percentile window.
2) Synthetic surge test: 3x normal QPS sustained for 5 minutes with expected warm-pool ramp; no more than 5% request failures and median latency within configured degradation target.
3) Quality regression bound: prompts from the canonical eval set must not drop more than 6% in average BLEU/embedding-similarity when routed to fallback variant.
4) Rollout gating: canary cannot proceed beyond 10% until synthetic tests and monitoring alerts are green for 2 consecutive runs.

Implementation constraints:
- The runtime must expose an ephemeral metric that marks "safety_gate_status" per model + kernel.
- Console must be able to read and surface that metric and allow manual override only with audit trail.

Potential blockers:
- Kernel changes may require low-level hardware vendor coordination (NVIDIA/AMD) which can delay delivery.
- Synthetic test harness needs integration with internal capacity simulator to produce reliable warm-pool behavior.
